summary: Owned units s0155–s0177 centre on Wang Xizhi’s break with Wang Shu, the Yonghe 11 tomb oath, and the retired life that follows. The oath itself supplies the only day-level date: 維永和十一年三月癸卯朔，九日辛亥. That is Eastern Jin Emperor Mu, era 永和 (a repeated era name; here the Jin Mu reign, not later homonyms), year 11. 癸卯 as day 1 makes 辛亥 day 9, so the Chinese date is internally consistent. Wikipedia’s concordance maps 永和十一年 to AD 355 and 三月朔癸卯 to 30 March; those Western day numbers follow the usual pre-1582 Julian presentation (Academia Sinica’s converter, which defaults to Julian before 1582, was not successfully queried). A one- or two-day Julian/proleptic-Gregorian shift in the 350s still leaves the event in AD 355, so year-precision westernYear AD 355 is the right conventional year under the proleptic Gregorian year-bound used here. 羲之既去官 and the Xu Mai / Xie An sequel are therefore on or after AD 355, not after 355. Wang Shu’s Yangzhou appointment is undated in s0156; the same book’s 穆帝紀 (永和十年二月) dates it to Yonghe 10, conventionally AD 354. Jiankang Shilu (month 3) and Zizhi Tongjian (month 1) compete on the month only; all three stay inside AD 354, so the derived year is kept and the month conflict is not collapsed. Parents are already dead by the tomb oath (on or before AD 355); the father’s death is further fixed to Xizhi’s youth and is not given a false birth-year. Laozi and Zhou Ren appear only as authorities invoked in the oath and are dated as retrospective reception, not as living activity. No owned unit states a birth; the 年在桑榆 remark is an age colour already captured in context, not a convertible sui figure. Active hints match these personal events and do not recycle posthumous or merely cited names.

The endpoint is the conventional Western year of Jin Mu Yonghe 11, not a guessed second bound.

Wikipedia’s Eastern Jin 永和 table gives year 11 as AD 355 and month-3 new moon as 30 March; identifying that day column as the usual Julian witness before 1582, proleptic Gregorian still keeps the Western year at 355. Year-precision AD 355 is therefore justified and is not a reign-year label stretched across a New Year hinge.

references.title: 永和 (东晋) - 维基百科，自由的百科全书
references.quote: 永和（345年—356年）是东晋皇帝晋穆帝司马聃的第一个年号，共计12年。
references.reason: Primary calendar reference for this job: identifies the ruler (晋穆帝司马聃), polity (东晋), and this 永和 era as years 1–12 = AD 345–356, so 永和十年 = AD 354 and 永和十一年 = AD 355. The same page’s concordance row for 永和十一年 lists 三月朔 as 癸卯 with Western 3/30, a Julian-style pre-1582 day number; day 9 辛亥 is then 7 April 355 Julian. Proleptic Gregorian stays inside AD 355 for that spring date, which is the convention used to accept the claims’ year-precision Western years.
